summary: A now-deprecated flat-API TypeScript HTTP client for Barkpark v1 that predates the workspace/project routing hierarchy. It exposes typed query, document, schema, and atomic mutation operations as a thin wrapper over fetch, with structured error handling.

intentions.title: Expose a strongly-typed JS surface for the Barkpark v1 HTTP API
intentions.evidence: types.ts defines DocumentEnvelope, Mutation union, QueryOptions, ErrorEnvelope etc.; client.ts wraps every v1 endpoint (query, getDocument, mutate, schemas) with generic type params; index.ts re-exports all for external consumers

intentions.title: Guarantee atomic multi-mutation transactions from the client side
intentions.evidence: client.ts mutate() batches Mutation[] into a single POST /v1/data/mutate call and documents 'Either all succeed or none do'; all single-shot helpers (create, patch, publish, delete) delegate through mutate()

intentions.title: Provide structured, catchable error types rather than raw HTTP failures
intentions.evidence: errors.ts BarkparkError parses the ErrorEnvelope.code discriminant union (not_found, rev_mismatch, conflict, etc.) and exposes .code/.status/.details; client.ts throws it on every non-2xx response

intentions.title: Keep client instances immutable and composable
intentions.evidence: client.ts withPerspective/withDataset/withToken each return a new Client sharing the same fetch impl — allows scoped sub-clients without mutating shared state

intentions.title: Allow injectable fetch for SSR and test environments
intentions.evidence: ClientConfig.fetch?: typeof fetch lets callers pass a custom implementation; client.ts falls back to globalThis.fetch and throws a clear error when neither is available

intentions.title: Mark a migration path away from the flat-URL API toward @barkpark/core
intentions.evidence: client.ts JSDoc @deprecated block explicitly names the workspace/project routing gap, confirms no monorepo importers, and directs consumers to @barkpark/core createClient
